source: NACA Report 1135, Tables I and II, gamma = 7/5
_comment_branch_pairs: An area ratio above 1 has a subsonic and a supersonic root. NACA prints A/A* as a function of M, not the reverse, and the two branches rarely land on the same printed value, so each pair is verified in two independent ways: the supersonic root against the exact printed area ratio at a tabulated Mach number, and the subsonic root against the interval given by two adjacent printed rows of Table I. Neither expectation is produced by RocketForge.

supersonic.bracket_source: NACA 1135 Table II, p.634 prints A/A* = 1.338 at M = 1.70. The area ratio is monotone increasing above M = 1, and 1.3398 > 1.338, so the supersonic root must lie above 1.70. Only rows actually read from the scan are cited, which is why the upper bound is the model ceiling rather than a tighter tabulated row.
